Incorporating the Beige Book, the FOMC’s June 10, 2020 statement is reinforced by broad-based weakness across districts: consumer spending fell amid retail closures; construction activity declined; agriculture deteriorated due to meat-processing plant disruptions; and firms cited employee health concerns while employment dropped widely. Pricing pressures were muted, with pronounced softness in airfare, hotel rooms, apparel, and commodity prices (notably oil), consistent with subdued inflation. Wage dynamics were mixed—some pay increases for essential/high-demand roles—but generally flat or declining elsewhere, underscoring slack. While policy actions (Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS purchases, robust repo and ON RRP operations) improved market functioning, the Beige Book’s real-economy signals point to persistent headwinds and considerable risks to the outlook. Overall, the Beige Book tilts the tone slightly more negative than the SLOOS-only read, though policy backstops still moderate the downside.
